name: VOID optical-flow warped noise (core)
plain: Moves Gaussian noise along RAFT optical flow so noise sticks to moving content across video frames, for temporally consistent refinement. Keeps Gaussian statistics when pixels merge or split using regaussianize. Ported in core from R. Burgert's code for the VOID pipeline.
math:
State per pixel: [dx,dy,ω,noise]. For each flow:
Expansion: nearest-neighbour remap by −flow. Shrink: scatter-add to new positions.
Regaussianize groups of duplicated pixels: n' = n/√count + (f − mean_group(f)), f ~ N(0,I).
Shrink channels: scat(n·ω)/√scat(ω²). ω renormalised to mean 1, ω=(ω+1e-5)^0.9999.
Frame done at internal size (resize_flow·resize_frames·H), output = area_pool(n, 1/D)·D with D=downscale_factor (default 32).

props.spectrum: white in space; correlated along flow in time
props.normalizes_variance: yes, statistically: regaussianize and ×D after area pool

label: from code

audit.note: void_noise_warp.py:287-288: order is reversed in the math. Code adds 1e-5 first, then raises to 0.9999.
